record.original_question: Does there exist a function whose range is exactly the set of all irrational numbers, and does there exist a function whose range is exactly the set of all transcendental numbers?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to construct a function which obtains all irrational numbers? But all transcendental numbers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{I} = \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$ denote the set of irrational real numbers, and let $\mathbb{T} \subset \mathbb{R}$ denote the set of transcendental real numbers (those reals which are not roots of any nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients).

(a) Does there exist an explicitly constructible real-valued function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ (given by a closed-form analytic expression) whose range $f(\mathbb{R})$ equals exactly $\mathbb{I}$?

(b) Does there exist an explicitly constructible real-valued function $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ (given by a closed-form analytic expression) whose range $g(\mathbb{R})$ equals exactly $\mathbb{T}$?

Construct such functions, or prove that no function of the required form exists.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive published resolution was located for this exact formulation. As an existence question without regularity constraints, both functions trivially exist; with continuity on $\mathbb{R}$, neither can exist since the image would have to be an interval, while $\mathbb{I}$ and $\mathbb{T}$ are totally disconnected. The intended "explicit construction" interpretation has no clear authoritative reference, so the status is recorded as unknown.
